goal: Act as Dr. Michael Torres: compute weighted Final_Grade and Letter_Grade for 35 SOC 101 students in the gradebook, adjudicate two grade appeals (Sullivan, Xu) in grade_dispute_decisions.csv, and write an assessment report to the chair with grade distributions, assignment-level stats by section, a benchmark of Course_Eval_Summary against the OpenIntro evals dataset, an at-risk summary, an essay rubric review with a Spring 2025 change, and a reflection.
delivered: output/ holds the updated SOC101_Fall2024_Gradebook.xlsx (correct Final_Grade/Letter_Grade, Sullivan 42.85% F, Mitchell 55.83% F), grade_dispute_decisions.csv (Sullivan Incomplete, Xu denied at 47.41% F), and SOC101_Fall2024_Assessment_Report.docx with 7 sections and tables. Grades, distributions, letters, signature and the reflection are correct.
what_went_wrong: The assignment table in report section 3 gives only mean and SD per component per section, with no medians. The eval benchmark (section 4) compares only 5 of the 10 Course_Eval_Summary items against the 4.175 OpenIntro mean, leaving out Learning objectives 3.7 and Would recommend 4.6. The essay review lists all six rubric dimensions but never ties the Midterm/Final essay score distributions to them. Mitchell is flagged at-risk only for grade < 70%: the report omits his two missing assignments and his 2024-11-07 family-emergency office-hours visit, although the agent had all this data.

failed_items.why: Section 3 table columns are 'Section A mean (SD)' / 'Section B mean (SD)' only. The agent computed no per-assignment medians and did not discuss variance from extreme performers, although it had the full Assignments sheet (step 5).

The agent fetched evals.csv (step 8) and read all of Course_Eval_Summary (step 6), but the benchmark table includes only 5 of the 10 items. Judge: no statement that Learning objectives 3.7 is below or Would recommend 4.6 is above the benchmark.

Section 6 names all six Berkeley categories and proposes a specific 0-4 scoring key. Judge: it never links the Midterm_Essay/Final_Essay distributions (A 75.07% vs B 70.52%, etc.) to performance on those dimensions.

Mitchell's 55.83% F is correct. However, at-risk is defined only as grade < 70%, so his two missing assignments and 4 absences plus 3 lates are not used as criteria. The OH visit is shown only as count 1, without the 11-07 family-emergency context, even though the log was read.
